bull.b: The 191 MW, 20-year Rockdale lease adds a substantial contracted infrastructure revenue stream beyond Bitcoin mining. Its long duration, expansion options, and projected high NOI margin could improve revenue visibility and diversify Riot’s business as delivery milestones are completed.

Low power cost is a durable competitive input in Bitcoin mining because electricity is central to production economics. Riot’s reported cost profile and 87% utilization support resilience against industry competition, although returns still depend on network conditions and Bitcoin economics.

The engineering segment provides operational capabilities that support Riot’s data center expansion while adding a growing source of revenue. Rising revenue, improved gross margin, and a largely data-center backlog indicate strengthening execution capacity and potential support for future deployments.

bear.b: Persistent negative profitability weakens Riot’s ability to fund expansion through internally generated earnings and reduces confidence in near-term capital efficiency. The return from 2024 profitability to deep 2025 and TTM losses also shows that earnings remain highly sensitive to operating conditions.

bear.t: Substantial cash burn and funding dependence
bear.b: Negative operating and free cash flow means Riot is consuming cash while pursuing a capital-intensive buildout. Continued development therefore depends on financing, asset sales, or other funding sources, which can constrain capital allocation and increase execution risk if project funding becomes less available.

bear.t: High exposure to Bitcoin mining volatility
bear.b: Riot’s core mining economics remain structurally exposed to volatile Bitcoin revenue and changing network competition, while electricity and infrastructure costs must be managed continuously. This dependence can create large swings in revenue and margins even when mining capacity and operational execution improve.
